artifacts.title: Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern

matches.evidence: …provide TE Lee with 14 days notice of the trial, as required by BCO 32-3. See BCO 32-10 (before proceeding to trial, courts ought to ascertain that their citations have been duly served). Based on these procedural errors, the…
See BCO 32-10 (before proceeding to trial, courts ought to ascertain that their citations have been duly served).

artifacts.synopsis: After Korean Eastern Presbytery tried, convicted, deposed, and excommunicated TE Eliot Lee, the SJC sustained his appeal and reversed the disposition and excommunication. The decisive reason was procedural: the record did not show timely service of the indictment/citations or the required 14-day trial notice, violating BCO 32-3, 32-7, and 32-10. Under BCO 42-9, the SJC rendered the decision it thought should have been made, finding no strong presumption of guilt under BCO 31-2 justified formal process; it added pastoral counsel, expressly not censure.

artifacts.title: Elevating a censure without a new trial under BCO 36

matches.evidence: Proposed amendment to BCO 36 providing for censure elevation without a wholly new trial was found to be ambiguous under the BCO.
